project_recovery.h.project_recovery_error: RecoveryError; all twelve error classes retained and name mapping preserved

project_recovery.h.project_recovery_encoded_size: project_recovery_encoded_size; checked size arithmetic and full bundle input validation

internal_helpers.crc32_update/crc32: CRC-32/IEEE, same reflected polynomial and envelope checksum zeroing rule

internal_helpers.bundle error translation: bundle_decode_failure maps Rust decoder OutOfMemory to FileError::OutOfMemory, Limit to Limit, and all other decoder errors to InvalidArgument; it always retains bundle_error and leaves native errors, bytes_written, published and directory_fsynced at their prepublication defaults. This is the explicitly authorized Rust allocation adaptation; all existing C category mappings remain unchanged.
internal_helpers.lstat and atomic publication: symlink_metadata selects regular replacement vs missing-path no-replace create; accepted vexel-platform-macos byte-path API owns native transaction and cleanup

contracts.bundle: ADR-0019 v1 limits and checksums are delegated to accepted vexel-project codec; no schema/limit reduction
contracts.recovery: ADR-0021 capsule remains separate from source and includes complete validated project bytes
contracts.ownership: inputs and decoded views borrow caller bytes; only save_as/save allocate the complete encoded publication buffer, with try_reserve in codec/recovery
contracts.filesystem: preserves symlink/nonregular rejection, regular replacement, no-replace races, native error classes, byte counts, commit state, and directory durability
contracts.platform: raw macOS Unix byte paths use safe OsStrExt adapter; no new unsafe code or unsupported OS code

adaptations: Rust slices make invalid nonempty pointer/null combinations unrepresentable; empty paths and byte-path NULs retain legacy invalid-argument behavior.
Decode returns Result<borrowed RecoveryView, RecoveryFailure> instead of mutating an out-parameter; failed decode has no observable partial view.
Safe native failure hooks are used only by private focused tests; every success path still executes the accepted native filesystem operation.
Safe Rust decoder allocation failure maps to FileError::OutOfMemory with the original bundle error and zero publication state; actual system OOM injection is intentionally not used.
